newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends little changed after lacklustre day.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends little changed after lacklustre day.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended little changed on Monday after a day of lacklustre trade.

Traders said the restart of some Nigerian crude production halted late last week had little impact on prices with good trans-atlantic and Asian demand seen for West Africa crude and world spot markets supported by "comfortable" refining margins.
June Brent last traded one cent weaker at $18.26 a barrel after holding in a 16 cent range over the day.
Analysts expect Brent to continue to trade within its recently established range for a while with good resistance at $18.64 capping any sharp gains.
Shell Nigeria said on Monday it would restart normal production from Forcados after reaching agreement with local communities to reopen oil flow stations at the weekend.
Shell said on Friday that 20 percent of its 475,000 barrels per day (bpd) Forcados output had been shut in because of ethnic strife in the region.
Gas oil futures ended steadier after holding in a narrow $1 range in lacklustre trade.
The May contract last traded 50 cents up at the day's high of $166 a tonne.
Brokers said the market steadied in late business as NYMEX heating oil prices moved moderately higher on short-covering ahead of Wednesday's expiry of the May contract.
NYMEX May heating oil last traded up 0.50 cent at 56.40 cents a gallon. Gasoline was down 0.30 at 62.20 cents a gallon and June WTI crude was down 14 cents at $19.85 a barrel.
